The ASOW follows a serpentine path with a unit cell length d = 2R, where R is the radius of the loops.
The difference in phase accumulation between segments B and B' in the unit cell, φ_b ≠ φ'_b, breaks the left-right symmetry and enables the SIP.
The authors derive five necessary conditions in Eq. (14) that must be satisfied for the ASOW to exhibit an SIP.
The SIP is an exceptional point of order three, where three Bloch eigenmodes coalesce.
At the SIP frequency ω_s, the characteristic equation has the simple form (ζ - ζ_s)^3(ζ - ζ_s^-1)^3 = 0.
The authors analyze a finite-length ASOW with N = 32 unit cells and show the frozen mode regime with dramatically enhanced field amplitudes in the middle of the structure.
The quality factor Q near the SIP frequency is high due to the frozen mode regime, but the ASOW does not behave as an isolated high-Q cavity compared to other exceptional point structures.
The authors use a coalescence parameter σ to quantify the degree of eigenvector coalescence at the SIP.
The ASOW is designed for a target SIP wavelength of 1550 nm, with a silicon waveguide of height 230 nm and width 430 nm.
The authors assume the ASOW is lossless and restrict the loop radius R ≥ 10 μm to minimize radiation losses.
